subject: Price cadence stability request — 3yr annuity + renewal parity safe harbor
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@straxsystems.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: kevin.martin@straxsystems.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing proposal questions — Strax (follow-up)

David — thanks for the proposal. We're excited by the model performance and the cost projections, but leadership asked for stronger price stability across years. Two asks: 1) a 3-year price lock with an annual uplift cap no greater than 5% (we need predictability for budget planning), and 2) a renewal-parity clause that prevents effective rate increases via mandatory feature add-ons.

Attached is an internal finance note that explains why they need this level of stability. Can your team confirm if those terms are conceivable for Strax at the commit levels in the proposal (1.2M tokens/month committed)?

Appreciate a quick confirmation — Elena

Attachments: Strax_finance_note.pdf
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing proposal questions — Strax (exec approval request)

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding Strax's request. Key asks: 3-year price lock, annual uplift cap <= 5%, and renewal-parity safe harbor (no hidden feature gating that changes effective unit economics). Current Commercial proposal offers a 3yr term with standard uplift language (annual CPI + up to 8% floor). We can stretch on term but need exec clearance to tighten uplift cap to 5% and include explicit renewal-parity language.

High-level tradeoffs:
- Impact to LTV calculus if uplift floor reduced from 8% to 5%: roughly 6–9% ARR erosion over 3 years at current utilization profiles (see quick calc in attached pricing summary).
- Upside: increases likelihood of a multi-year commit and counters competitor bids in procurement.

Attachments: Strax_3yr_pricing_summary_v2.pdf, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Requesting: 1) approval to offer 5% uplift cap, 2) signoff to add a renewal parity clause limited to features tied to premium performance tiers (we would carve out brand-new product modules), and 3) permission to provide a one-time onboarding credit of $40k to offset migration costs.

Can you approve or propose edits?
— David
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jun 2028 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing proposal questions — Strax (exec approval request)

Thanks David — reviewed the attached summary. I support tightening the uplift cap to 5% conditioned on: (a) Strax committing to an annual minimum consumption band (they already proposed 1.2M tokens/month — mark as committed), and (b) a clause that allows us to renegotiate pricing if utilization exceeds committed bands by >80% for two consecutive quarters (to protect against runaway unit economics).

On renewal parity: acceptable if we define "parity" narrowly — it should apply only to SKU price per token and not to add-on premium features launched after contract signature. We should include a defined list of premium features at signing and reserve the right to price new, materially different modules separately.

I also endorse the $40k onboarding credit but recommend we structure it as a one-time rebate tied to a 12-month payment schedule (i.e., paid back if they churn within 12 months).

If Lauren signs off on those conditions, I'll draft redlines for legal and ops to bake into the T&Cs.

— Marissa
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@straxsystems.com>
Cc: kevin.martin@straxsystems.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing proposal questions — Strax (exec approval request)

All — thanks for the clear summary and diligence. I approve the concession package with the following executive conditions (documenting here so legal has clear guardrails):

1) Offer: 3-year term with a guaranteed annual uplift cap of 5% (flat cap on CPI/annual adjustments).
2) Commitments: Customer must sign an annual minimum committed usage of 1.2M tokens/month. Failure to meet 75% of committed usage in any 12-month period will trigger a true-up at the higher of contract price or list price pro-rated.
3) Renegotiation trigger: If actual average monthly usage exceeds committed band by >80% for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may open a pricing review; this preserves capacity and margin.
4) Renewal-parity safe harbor: Include a clause that protects customers from stealth FX via mandatory add-ons — applies only to price-per-token and named integrations listed in Schedule A. New premium products launched post-signing are excluded. Legal to draft Schedule A enumerating the initial premium list.
5) Onboarding credit: Approve $40k rebate to offset migration, structured as a 12-month amortized credit that is clawed back if Strax terminates before 12 months.

David/Marissa: please route to Legal (contracts@redwood.com) with these bullet points and attach the two files referenced. Ask legal to prepare a short amendment and a Schedule A that we can show Strax this week.

I will authorize Deal Desk to finalize pricing with these guardrails.

— Lauren Bishop, VP Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
